Every row renders a card. No error kind returns a bare string, because `suppressAssistantResponse: true` is set on every `ToolResponse` this tool returns, so a kind without a card would leave the customer with no answer at all and would hand the model the delivery question that [ADR-002](../../../adrs/ADR-002-deterministic-delivery-status-rendering.md) reserves for the card. The escalation marker is a separate axis: only `unavailable`, `timeout` and a customer conflict escala…

`defineTmsTool` in `apps/api/src/tools/defineTmsTool.ts` takes a HAL Engine `ToolDefinition`, a projection, a request (`method` and `call`) and the escalation marker from #24. It returns a `{definition, execute}` pair. On success `execute` returns `JSON.stringify(project(response))`. The projection is the only way the TMS response gets out, so a field the projection does not name never leaves the process. At definition time the factory throws for `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` and names the EU AI Act (E5) human-oversight requirement. An error carrying one of the nine `TmsError` kinds maps through `ESCALATION_BY_KIND`, a `Record<TmsErrorKind, EscalationTrigger | null>`. A kind with no row fails typecheck, just as a `switch` with no `default` would. The repo's lint rules (`complexity`, …
That is the deterministic, factory-fired trigger the escalation spec's FR-004 expects. Every other kind returns `{"error":kind}` with no message text. Any other error propagates unchanged.

# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

Answers the customer's questions "Hvornår bliver min booking XXXXX leveret?" / "When will my booking XXXXX be delivered?" by looking up the delivery status of a specific booking reference. The tool answers only about the booking whose reference was supplied; it never enumerates or lists bookings. The answer is always a deterministic delivery card — the model never phrases a delivery time or status. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_7b75ccc7-9e83-4505-ac6e-f13070df6b0a), [from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_4c37e3b5-2d8c-45eb-88d3-dbc55c9b3a65))

## Input Schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "booking_reference": {"type": "string"}
  },
  "required": ["booking_reference"]
}
```

# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

## Input Schema

One required property: `booking_reference`. No customer id, no company id — scope is resolved from the authenticated session by the resolver of #18, never from a model-supplied argument.

**Pattern routing** (decided by the pattern of `booking_reference`, after trimming surrounding whitespace and upper-casing it, so `olt-2024-0001 ` routes as `OLT-2024-0001`): ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_70b73bf0-839e-489b-bf55-3730d99be632), [from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_912eac3d-6b9d-4909-b850-04ee4569dd5c))

## Input Schema

| Pattern             | Route          | TMS endpoint                                        |
| ------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `^OLT-\d{4}-\d{4}$` | Order path     | `GET /orders/{idOrNumber}` (scope `orders:read`)    |
| `^SHP-\d{4}-\d{6}$` | Shipment path  | `GET /shipments/{idOrRef}` (scope `shipments:read`) |

[5] "specs/support-agent-tms-tool-contract/contracts/get-booking-status.md" section 5:
# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

## Input Schema

**Who may see a booking** (decided 2026-10-15). OLT's API names two customers on every order and shipment: `ordererCustomerNumber` booked it and `customerNumber` pays for it, often the same customer but not always (OLT's guide names a Netto booking paid by Salling). The booking is the signed-in customer's when the resolver's `customerNumber` is either one. On the order path the order decides for its shipments, which the published API returns without customer numbers; a shipment that does name a payer or orderer other than its order's means the TMS contradicts itself, and the tool escalates `customer_scope_conflict`. Anyone else's booking answers exactly as an unknown reference does. `defineTmsTool` requires this check from every TMS tool as its `ownership` option.

[6] "specs/support-agent-tms-tool-contract/contracts/get-booking-status.md" section 6:
# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

## Output Projection

The tool returns a `ToolResponse` with `suppressAssistantResponse: true` and `clientMessages` carrying one `entry_upsert` frame per card, `{"type": "entry_upsert", "index": n, "entry": {"role": "delivery_card", …}}`; HAL Engine numbers each and stores it with the conversation. The examples below show each frame's `entry`. `defineTmsTool` builds the frames and the `ToolResponse`; the tool supplies only the card entries. The `result` string carries a minimal projection for the conversation transcript only. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_eb893133-1fdf-46a1-8d89-263ddac9c091))

# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

## Output Projection

### Order path projection (fields sent per shipment card in `clientMessages`)

| Card field           | Source field (TMS order response) | Notes                                 |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `orderNumber`        | `orderNumber`                     | The heading FR-102 renders            |
| `shipmentReference`  | `shipments[n].shipmentReference`  | SHP-format reference                  |
| `statusCode`         | `shipments[n].status`             | One of the ten status codes           |
| `deliveryDate`       | `shipments[n].deliveryDate`       | Used for booked window                |
| `deliveryTimeFrom`   | `shipments[n].deliveryTimeFrom`   | Used for booked window                |
| `deliveryTimeTo`     | `shipments[n].deliveryTimeTo`     | Used for booked window                |
| `eta`                | `shipments[n].stops.delivery.eta` | UTC; null falls back to booked window |
| `actualDeliveryTime` | `shipments[n].actualDeliveryTime` | Set for LEVERET/DELVIST_LEVERET       |
| `deviationCode`      | `shipments[n].deviationCode`      | Optional; triggers deviation line     |

# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

## Worked Request/Response Pairs

### Data integrity conflict — order path

TMS returns the order, but a shipment names a payer or orderer other than the order's. The disagreement signals a data integrity problem; the tool escalates `customer_scope_conflict` to a human and renders the error card rather than the shipment cards. A shipment that names no customer takes its order's, since the published API returns an order's shipments without one.

**Tool result (`ToolResponse`):** the error card, with the escalation recorded alongside it:

```json
{
  "suppressAssistantResponse": true,
  "clientMessages": [
    {
      "role": "delivery_card",
      "variant": "error",
      "escalated": true
    }
  ],
  "result": "{\"error\":\"customer_scope_conflict\",\"escalation\":\"customer_scope_conflict\"}"
}
```

The escalation rides with it under its own trigger, `customer_scope_conflict`. The card is required, not optional: `suppressAssistantResponse: true` is set on every response this tool returns, so an escalation without a card would leave the customer staring at a turn that produced nothing. The card names no order, shipment, customer or status, so the escalating branch still reveals only that the lookup did not complete.

# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

Answers the customer's questions "Hvornår bliver min booking XXXXX leveret?" / "When will my booking XXXXX be delivered?" by looking up the delivery status of a specific booking reference. The tool answers only about the booking whose reference was supplied; it never enumerates or lists bookings. The answer is always a deterministic delivery card — the model never phrases a delivery time or status. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_7b75ccc7-9e83-4505-ac6e-f13070df6b0a), [from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_4c37e3b5-2d8c-45eb-88d3-dbc55c9b3a65))

## Input Schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "booking_reference": {"type": "string"}
  },
  "required": ["booking_reference"]
}
```

[5] "specs/support-agent-tms-tool-contract/contracts/get-booking-status.md" section 5:
# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

## Input Schema

**Who may see a booking** (decided 2026-10-15). OLT's API names two customers on every order and shipment: `ordererCustomerNumber` booked it and `customerNumber` pays for it, often the same customer but not always (OLT's guide names a Netto booking paid by Salling). The booking is the signed-in customer's when the resolver's `customerNumber` is either one. On the order path the order decides for its shipments, which the published API returns without customer numbers; a shipment that does name a payer or orderer other than its order's means the TMS contradicts itself, and the tool escalates `customer_scope_conflict`. Anyone else's booking answers exactly as an unknown reference does. `defineTmsTool` requires this check from every TMS tool as its `ownership` option.

# Tool Contract: `get_booking_status`

## Worked Request/Response Pairs

### Data integrity conflict — order path

TMS returns the order, but a shipment names a payer or orderer other than the order's. The disagreement signals a data integrity problem; the tool escalates `customer_scope_conflict` to a human and renders the error card rather than the shipment cards. A shipment that names no customer takes its order's, since the published API returns an order's shipments without one.

**Tool result (`ToolResponse`):** the error card, with the escalation recorded alongside it:

```json
{
  "suppressAssistantResponse": true,
  "clientMessages": [
    {
      "role": "delivery_card",
      "variant": "error",
      "escalated": true
    }
  ],
  "result": "{\"error\":\"customer_scope_conflict\",\"escalation\":\"customer_scope_conflict\"}"
}
```

The escalation rides with it under its own trigger, `customer_scope_conflict`. The card is required, not optional: `suppressAssistantResponse: true` is set on every response this tool returns, so an escalation without a card would leave the customer staring at a turn that produced nothing. The card names no order, shipment, customer or status, so the escalating branch still reveals only that the lookup did not complete.
